architecture_model.center_hypothesis: The architecture favors code-derived governance (routing heuristics, lint scripts, host-derivation) over infrastructure or declarative configuration, claiming this reduces complexity; however, each of these choices merely relocates complexity to a less auditable substrate — heuristic scoring functions, un-tested lint scripts, and implicit configuration in routing code — creating a system that is self-describing but whose self-description cannot be independently verified.

key_assumptions.assumption: Weighted token-overlap scoring is more transparent than NLU because developers can mentally simulate the scoring function
evidence: No user study or routing-explain mechanism exists
Asymmetric weights (name > description) create a non-linear scoring surface impossible to mentally simulate past n>5 tools
No tie-breaking strategy for convergent scores

key_assumptions.assumption: Host-header derivation eliminates configuration management complexity
evidence: Derivation logic IS configuration — written in code with global blast radius
No Host-header edge case handling evidence (IPv6, X-Forwarded-Host, multi-value)
Per-tenant isolation is sacrificed, not achieved

key_assumptions.assumption: Lint script existence implies effective boundary enforcement
evidence: No recall metrics or false-negative test suite for the lint script
Dynamic imports, computed paths, and eval bypass lint by construction
Without a regression suite, recall decays as codebase evolves

architecture_invariants: Filesystem-based routing imposes strict dynamic-route precedence ordering — catch-all must always be lowest priority
Module boundaries are enforced solely by a custom lint script at lint time, not by runtime isolation
API contract must be machine-verifiable in CI, not just by convention

competing_interpretations.interpretation: Token-overlap scoring is chosen for infrastructure simplicity (no model server, no embedding pipeline), not for developer-transparency. The transparency narrative is a post-hoc justification for a pragmatic cost-avoidance decision.
evidence: No transparency tooling (routing explainer, confidence display) exists
The scoring function's two-weight design is never documented in external docs, only in a source-code comment
NLU-based routing with embedding visualization could provide MORE transparency via nearest-neighbor inspection

competing_interpretations.interpretation: The system is not 'self-describing' but rather has a tight circular dependency between code and documentation: code generates metadata, metadata describes code, and the CI-check verifies they match — but no independent oracle exists to detect shared bugs in both code and the doc-generation logic.
evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md capability counts are derived from code AND verified by docs:check which also reads the same code
No external specification or contract test exists that is independent of the implementation
A bug in code causes a bug in docs that passes CI because both derive from the same source of truth

competing_interpretations.interpretation: The architecture's 'single deployment with agent-readiness' is simultaneously over-engineered for a monolith and under-engineered for a distributed system: it has agent-discovery infrastructure (A2A, OAuth metadata, NLWeb) but no runtime isolation between agents, allowing any agent capability to be shadowed or interfered with by any other via the shared routing surface.
evidence: A2A endpoint and conventional REST share the same /api paths without network-level isolation
Lint-only enforcement cannot prevent one agent's tool from affecting another's routing scores
The architectural tension section acknowledges but does not address dual-interpretation pressure on the API surface

challenge_record.target: Token-overlap routing is 'deliberately transparent' so developers can predict routing behavior
challenge_record.challenge: Weighted multi-field token-overlap scoring is not meaningfully transparent — it is a threshold-free heuristic with implicit tie-breaking that developers must empirically probe, not mentally simulate
challenge_record.method: 移除测试, 假设翻转, 边界测试, 时间测试
evidence: 移除测试: The transparency claim has no test evidence for developer comprehension — no user study, no routing-explain endpoint, no tie-breaking documentation. The only evidence is a source-code comment asserting transparency.

假设翻转: If NLU embedding similarity were used, a developer could inspect nearest-neighbor clusters in embedding space — a visualizable structure. Token-overlap with asymmetric weights (name > description) has no such visualization; the scoring function is a private heuristic.

边界测试: With n tools sharing k overlapping tokens (e.g., get_shipping_status / get_shipping_eta / get_shipping_tracking) the weighted overlap converges, making routing effectively non-deterministic from the developer's perspective. No evidence of tie-breaking strategy.

时间测试: As tool inventory grows, the overlap matrix density increases O(n²). A heuristic that is simple at n=10 becomes opaque at n=100 — every new tool shifts scores for all existing tools, producing emergent non-local behavior no developer can predict.
challenge_record.model_delta: Transparency is a claimed property, not an algorithmic property. The model should be updated: token-overlap offers operational simplicity (no model server, no embedding infrastructure) but its routing behavior is opaque in the same practical sense as NLU — developers must test, not predict.

challenge_record.target: Host-header-derived metadata eliminates per-deployment configuration drift
challenge_record.challenge: Host-derivation does not eliminate configuration — it embeds configuration in routing code, which is harder to version, review, and isolate per tenant than declarative config files
challenge_record.method: 移除测试, 假设翻转, 边界测试, 时间测试
evidence: 移除测试: No test evidence for the derivation logic itself — only tests for the output metadata documents. A bug in the shared derivation logic affects ALL hosts simultaneously; per-deployment config files isolate blast radius per tenant.

假设翻转: Static config per deployment can be diffed, reviewed independently, and rolled back per host. Host-derivation in code means any change to the derivation function affects apex, www, api, va identically — the blast radius is global, not per-tenant.

边界测试: Unusual Host headers (IPv6 literals, non-standard ports, X-Forwarded-Host chaining, multi-value Host) must all be handled in the derivation logic. Per-deployment config never encounters this — the config IS the source of truth, derived from nothing.

时间测试: As origin count grows (staging × region × canary × production), the derivation function accumulates conditionals and edge cases, eventually becoming a routing table embedded in code — harder to audit, test, and modify than a declarative config file.
challenge_record.model_delta: The tradeoff is mischaracterized. The actual tradeoff is: single deployment simplicity vs. per-tenant isolation — not 'config drift eliminated.' The host-derivation approach eliminates config files but introduces a shared configuration surface in code with global blast radius and Host-header attack surface.

challenge_record.target: Lint-only boundary enforcement gives fast feedback and zero runtime cost
challenge_record.challenge: The lint script has zero test evidence for recall — 'fast feedback' is meaningless if the script misses actual violations, and the admission that runtime violations are possible reveals a governance hole, not a tradeoff
challenge_record.method: 移除测试, 假设翻转, 边界测试, 时间测试
evidence: 移除测试: The interpretation cites the script's existence as evidence of enforcement. No test evidence for the lint script's own correctness — no recall metric, no benchmark against known violations, no false-negative test suite. Existence ≠ effectiveness.

假设翻转: Lint-only enforcement creates negative trust — developers see 'boundaries enforced' in CI and stop reasoning about module isolation. A lint script with unknown recall (potentially missing dynamic imports, computed paths, eval-based loading) is worse than no enforcement because it provides misplaced confidence.

边界测试: Every computed import (await import(pathVar)), every eval-based module access, every monkey-patch at runtime bypasses static analysis entirely. These are not edge cases — they are architectural bypasses the governance model cannot address by design.

时间测试: As the codebase grows, lint scripts must be maintained to cover new module-access patterns. Without a regression test suite for the lint script itself, recall decays monotonically with codebase evolution. The governance is itself ungoverned.
challenge_record.model_delta: The claim that lint-only enforcement is a 'design decision' rather than an acknowledged gap is incorrect. The model should reclassify this: lint-only boundary enforcement is an intentional omission with acknowledged blind spots (dynamic loading, runtime access), not a positive design choice. The tradeoff section admits the weakness but the model section presents it as ownership/extension — this framing inconsistency should be resolved.

design_space.decision: Tool routing uses transparent token-overlap scoring instead of NLU
design_space.chosen: Token-overlap score over tool names + descriptions, with name hits weighted higher than description hits
design_space.why_chosen: Deliberately transparent so developers can predict routing behavior; name-precision ensures 'chokepoint status' lands on get_chokepoint_status, not on every tool whose prose mentions shipping
design_space.why_rejected: Deliberately transparent so developers can predict routing behavior; name-precision ensures 'chokepoint status' lands on get_chokepoint_status, not on every tool whose prose mentions shipping
evidence: api/_agent-tool-suggest.ts: 'Deliberately not NLU — a transparent token-overlap score over the same names + descriptions tools/list publishes anonymously'
Name hits outweigh description hits

design_space.decision: OAuth/agent-readiness metadata derived from Host header at runtime instead of static configuration
design_space.chosen: resource/issuer + endpoint origin computed per-request from Host header
design_space.why_chosen: Single deployment serves multiple origins; PRM and AS metadata must stay self-consistent per host without separate config files or deployments
design_space.why_rejected: Single deployment serves multiple origins; PRM and AS metadata must stay self-consistent per host without separate config files or deployments
evidence: api/_agent-metadata.ts: 'Both derive their resource/issuer + endpoint origin from the request Host so PRM and AS metadata stay self-consistent per host'

design_space.decision: Module boundaries and API contract enforced by custom lint scripts, not by framework or runtime
design_space.chosen: Dedicated scripts/lint-boundaries.mjs and scripts/enforce-sebuf-api-contract.mjs run in CI
design_space.why_chosen: Single deployment with self-managed topology; architectural boundary governance via dedicated lint scripts ensures code-level constraints without infrastructure complexity
design_space.why_rejected: Single deployment with self-managed topology; architectural boundary governance via dedicated lint scripts ensures code-level constraints without infrastructure complexity
evidence: package.json scripts: lint:boundaries, lint:api-contract
'Module boundaries enforced by lint-boundaries.mjs'
'Architectural boundary governance via dedicated lint scripts, not convention alone'

complexity_drivers: Catch-all [...notfound].ts must exist for 404 handling but its lowest-precedence constraint creates subtle ordering dependencies — adding a new dynamic route could accidentally shadow or be shadowed by existing routes

Agent-readiness (A2A, OAuth metadata, NLWeb tool routing) occupies the same API surface as conventional REST endpoints, creating dual interpretation pressure — the same /api path is both a human-facing API and an agent-discovery endpoint

Documentation ownership rule demands manual update when architecture changes, but capability counts are auto-derived from code — creating friction between 'hand-edit when topology changes' and 'auto-generate from code'
